A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GNN expressivity study. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching renamed concepts and relocated material.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original experiments on synthetic LCQP and MI-LCQP instances, including fitting errors, model-capacity studies, and generalization results.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendices D and G report original synthetic and benchmark experiments, runtime measurements, and analysis of QPLIB instances under coefficient quantization.

M1.justification: Section 2 changes LCQP messages from edge-weighted node functions to functions receiving both node features and edge weights, a formulation already used for MI-LCQPs in v1. New Appendix E introduces a substantive QCQP adaptation with hyperedges, learned constraint-variable edge states, and additional update equations.

E1.justification: v2 retains generic synthetic LCQP and MI-LCQP experiments and adds portfolio optimization, SVM optimization, the Maros-Meszaros convex-QP collection, and QPLIB mixed-integer instances. It also studies quantized QPLIB inputs. The QCQP extension is theoretical, without corresponding experiments.

E2.justification: v2 adds OSQP as a direct runtime comparator in Table 1; v1 uses solvers for labels without this comparison. PIQP supplies benchmark labels in Appendix G.5 and is not an evaluated competing predictor.

E3.justification: New protocols include application-specific instance generation, scaling and selecting 136 successfully solved Maros-Meszaros instances, fitting 73 QPLIB instances, and quantization at steps 0.1, 0.5, and 1. The runtime experiment uses 1,000 synthetic problems, four GNN batch sizes, and an OSQP relative-error target of 0.001. Original synthetic sampling and generalization splits are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix D.2 adds a structural sensitivity analysis testing how quantization changes WL-defined solvability and analyzability on QPLIB. Table 1 adds batch-size sensitivity of inference time. The original embedding-size, sample-size, and generalization analyses remain; moving generalization to Appendix G is not a new analysis.

E5.justification: v2 adds shaded bands to Figure 3, error bars to Figure 4, and explicitly reported timing standard deviations in Table 1. Neither version specifies seeds or repeated-run counts, and v2 does not define the plotted bands or bars, so additional runs cannot be established.

E6.justification: Figure 4's numerical curves change, and v2 adds application, benchmark, timing, and quantization results. Table 2 reports 19 of 96 original instances classified as GNN-insolvable, increasing to 63 after integer rounding. Table 1 reports OSQP at 4.48 ms versus GNN at 53.62 ms for batch size 1 and 0.089 ms for batch size 1,000. These are new comparisons, not improvements over v1 results.

T1.justification: v2 broadens graph domains beyond positive-semidefinite Q, localizes convexity assumptions, and adds an explicit nonconvex counterexample. Appendix E introduces QCQP definitions, an associated WL algorithm, approximation theorems, and separation proofs. Existing approximation proofs become substantially more explicit. GNN-analyzability and GNN-solvability retain the earlier MP-tractability and unfoldability conditions under new names.

C1.justification: The central positive convex-LCQP and qualified MI-LCQP expressivity claims remain. v2 makes convexity and mixed-integer nonuniversality explicit in the abstract, adds nonconvex failure to the stated contributions, emphasizes efficiently checkable favorable subclasses, and mentions its QCQP extension in the introduction.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix D add substantial interpretation of symmetry, practical subclass frequency, diagnostic checks, and possible remedies using additional features or stronger GNNs. New benchmark discussion acknowledges fitting difficulties. Section 5 also introduces a broad runtime-superiority interpretation, although Table 1 shows slower GNN times at batch sizes 1 and 10.

D1.justification: v2 adds a link to the work's own code, detailed portfolio and SVM generation recipes, and Maros-Meszaros scaling, PIQP labeling, and instance-selection information. Existing Python/TensorFlow versions, optimizer, learning-rate schedule, GPU, loss, and parameter counts are retained.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands positioning through an explicit comparison with Wu et al.'s concurrent QCQP work, distinguishing graph representations and mixed-integer coverage. It also introduces substantive connections to higher-order and k-hop GNNs, random features, and algorithm unrolling, alongside references supporting the new benchmarks and solvers.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are substantially rewritten, Section 4 reorganizes and renames its central concepts, and a new practical discussion subsection is introduced. Generalization discussion moves to the appendix, the former Appendices C and D exchange roles, and implementation material moves from Appendix E to G.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, and Figure 2 repurposes an earlier appendix example for the continuous-case discussion. v2 adds application and benchmark plots plus timing and quantization tables, introduces uncertainty graphics, and revises Figure 4's axes and display. The generalization plots and parameter-count table are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: The real-benchmark fits and QPLIB quantization analysis make practical limitations assessable beyond v1's generic synthetic experiments. More explicit proofs, implementation recipes, and a code link substantially improve verifiability. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses: undefined uncertainty graphics, Figure 2 retaining integer constraints in an example discussed as continuous, and runtime claims broader than Table 1 supports.
